compiled_state.author: Joe Oakhart
compiled_state.description:
## Problem

Every rebar LLM gate resolves its model-class table to nothing and falls back to rebar's built-in direct-Anthropic defaults. This deployment holds no Anthropic credentials, so a gate either returns INDETERMINATE or fails outright with "Could not resolve authentication method". The close gate's completion verifier fails the same way, which is why closing a ticket currently needs `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` set by hand on the command line.

Reproduced against the working tree with rebar's own resolver.

```
discovered project config: (PosixPath('/Users/joeoakhart/agentic-dev-platform/rebar.toml'), 'toml')
llm section            : {}
verify section         : {'require_plan_review_for_close': True, ...}
```

Reproduced again inside a git worktree holding only tracked content, which is what a gate reads.

```
discovered project config: None
llm section            : {}
verify section         : {}
```

## Cause

Two facts compound. Either alone would be harmless.

**The Bedrock routing lives where rebar never looks.** `config/local/rebar-review.toml` holds the `[llm]` table, but `_discover_project_config` only accepts `$REBAR_CONFIG`, the nearest `rebar.toml`, or a `pyproject.toml` carrying a `[tool.rebar]` table. That path is none of those, so the table is reachable only by naming it explicitly through `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE`. Only the `inv` review wrappers and the compose review worker do that, so every other entry point routes at the defaults.

**The project config is untracked.** `rebar.toml` is excluded through `.git/info/exclude`. A running gate pins its code read-root to an attested git snapshot, and the snapshot has no untracked files, so discovery returns `None` there and both `llm` and `verify` resolve empty. The gates the project believes it enforces are absent from the root the gate itself reads.

`rebar.toml` also takes precedence over `pyproject.toml` in the walk, so while it exists it shadows any tracked config regardless of what that config declares.

## Approach

Move the project's rebar config into a tracked file rebar already discovers.

- Add `[tool.rebar.verify]` to `pyproject.toml` carrying the three gate flags currently in `rebar.toml`, namely `require_plan_review_for_close`, `require_plan_review_for_claim` and `require_completion_verification_for_close`, all true.
- Add `[tool.rebar.llm]` to `pyproject.toml` carrying the retry widening and the three Bedrock model classes currently in `config/local/rebar-review.toml`.
- Delete the local `rebar.toml`. It is untracked, so this is not a repository change, but it must go or it shadows `pyproject.toml` in the discovery walk. The `.git/info/exclude` entry stays so a recreated file is still never committed.
- Keep `config/local/rebar-review.toml`. The compose review worker names it by container path and two test modules read it, so removing it is a wider change than this ticket. It layers over the discovered table through `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` and declares identical values, so the merge is a no-op.
- Guard the duplication with a test asserting the two model-class tables are equal, so they cannot drift.

- Correct the README passage that presents `config/local/rebar-review.toml` as the file rebar reads. It is read only when something names it explicitly, so the passage sends a reader to a file the gate cannot discover. Name the tracked `pyproject.toml` table as the discovered source and keep the container and host wrappers described as the explicit-pointer callers they are.

`REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` stops being required. `tasks.py` keeps setting it because the layering is harmless and removing it is out of scope here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pyproject.toml` declares `[tool.rebar.verify]` with the same three flags the local `rebar.toml` carried, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_rebar_review_config.py -k tracked_project_config`
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` declares a `[tool.rebar.llm]` model-class table equal to the one in `config/local/rebar-review.toml`, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_rebar_review_config.py -k tracked_project_config`
- [ ] rebar's own discovery resolves a non-empty `llm` and `verify` section from a tree containing only tracked files and no `rebar.toml`, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_rebar_review_config.py -k discovers_the_tracked_config`
- [ ] The existing rebar review config tests still pass, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_rebar_review_config.py tests/unit/test_review_tiers.py`
- [ ] `README.md` states that the tracked `pyproject.toml` table is what the gates discover, so a reader is not sent to a file the gate cannot see

## Testing

Two tests are added to `tests/unit/test_rebar_review_config.py`.

The first parses `pyproject.toml` and asserts its `[tool.rebar.llm] model_classes` table equals the one already parsed from `config/local/rebar-review.toml`, and that the three verify flags are present and true. This is the anti-drift guard for the intentional duplication.

The second is the regression test for the defect. It builds a directory holding only a copy of `pyproject.toml` plus a `.git` marker to stop the upward walk, then calls `rebar.config.read_reserved_section` against it and asserts both sections resolve non-empty. This reproduces the attested-snapshot read that returns `None` today. Against the current tree it fails, because no tracked file carries either table.

Commands:

- `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_rebar_review_config.py tests/unit/test_review_tiers.py`
- `.venv/bin/ruff check services tests`

file_impact.reason: Add [tool.rebar.verify] and [tool.rebar.llm] so rebar discovers the gate config from tracked content
Assert the tracked tables match rebar-review.toml and that discovery resolves them from a tree with no rebar.toml
Point readers at the tracked pyproject table as the config the gates discover
